title: A friend's question
hook: on the Emmaus road the risen Jesus asks 'What things?' and lets two sad friends tell it all
tomorrow: why do the Buddha's teachings open with 'Thus have I heard'?

segments.voice: Rahula asked his father how, and was given the steady earth, then one breath, never ordered. Passing it on to a child is one thing. A grown friend with a hard question is another.
screen: `ONE BREATH, ON STEADY GROUND.` → `NOW, A FRIEND'S QUESTION.`

segments.voice: Can I ask you something kind of personal? The text lands, and before the question even arrives, you're drafting the answer. Luke's Gospel has a stranger who does the opposite. On the same day the tomb is found empty, two followers of Jesus are walking to a village called Emmaus, talking it over, sad. A stranger falls in beside them. Luke tells us it's Jesus, risen, but their eyes are held so they don't know him. He asks what they're discussing. One of them, Cleopas, says: are you the only stranger in Jerusalem who hasn't heard? And Jesus says: "What things?" It happened to him. So why ask?
screen: `DRAFTING THE ANSWER EARLY.` → `TWO SAD FRIENDS ON THE ROAD.` → `A STRANGER: WHAT THINGS?` → `IT HAPPENED TO HIM. WHY ASK?`

segments.voice: Because he lets them tell it. All of it: the prophet they followed, the cross, the hope they'd had. "But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel." The women at the empty tomb, the confusion. Only when they've told the whole story does he speak, opening the scriptures to them as they walk. At the village he makes as if to go on, and they ask him to stay. At the table he breaks the bread, and they know him, and he's gone. Then they say to each other: "Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way?" In Luke's story, the risen Christ walks beside people on the road, and is known in the breaking of bread, the same thing he did with bread at the Last Supper. And notice the order. Question first. Listening second. Speaking third. Bread last. So when a friend asks what you believe, the story's answer is a question back: what things? What's behind the question? Let them tell it all before you say much at all.
screen: `HE LETS THEM TELL IT ALL.` · `THEN HE OPENS THE SCRIPTURES.` · `KNOWN IN THE BREAKING OF BREAD.` · `QUESTION, LISTEN, SPEAK, BREAD.` · then, large: `LISTEN FIRST.`

segments.voice: For this sit, just listen. Pick one sound around you, a fan, traffic, a bird, your own breath, and follow it all the way to its end before you name it. When your mind starts drafting a reply to something, come back to listening.
A friend's question: a door someone opens to you, met on the Emmaus road with a question back, and a long listen.
Pocket this: listen first, the way the stranger on the road asked, What things? Talk soon.

fork.setup: your aunt, recently widowed, says over lunch, 'i don't know what i believe anymore.' you have a lot of thoughts. what fits the Emmaus road?
options: ask what's been happening, and let her tell it all before you say much.
share the most comforting belief you know right away, so she isn't stuck.
